I added `send_text(text, name)` to `src/flask/helpers.py` and exported it from `flask`, and all tests pass (491 passed, 3 skipped); it passes the file name to `send_file` by position rather than as `download_name=`, because a hook reported that another agent is renaming that parameter to `filename`, and this way the call works under either name.

+def send_text(text: str, name: str) -> Response:
+    """Send a string to the client as a downloadable plain text file.
+
+    The text is encoded as UTF-8 and sent with :func:`send_file` using
+    the ``text/plain`` mimetype.
+
+    :param text: The text content of the file.
+    :param name: The name browsers will use when saving the file.
+    """
+    # The download name is passed positionally so the call does not depend
+    # on the name of send_file's download name parameter.
+    return send_file(io.BytesIO(text.encode("utf-8")), "text/plain", True, name)
